To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a population of virus particles with different electrophoretic mobilities can be detected in plant extracts by NEWeB, that two different virus strains can be distinguished by NEWeB in mixed infections, and that helper component proteinase can be detected in particles from PPV-infected leaves by NEWeB.

a combination of native electophoresis and immunoblotting (NEWeB) is an efficient tool to characterize nucleoprotein particles and related complexes in plant extracts and that the NEWeB technique can be used for the analysis of virus particles from single infections, as well as from mixed infections of different virus species or strains.
a combination of native electroporesis and Western immunoblotting is a powerful method for the analysis of different forms of virus particles in infected plant tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new techniques to study the structure and function of plant viruses.
the characterization of different forms and functions of nucleoprotein complexes of plant pathogenic viruses.
the characterization of potyviral particles in infected plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NEWeB technique provides a simple, fast, and reliable tool for the characterization of potyviruses, their particles, and their nucleoprotein complexes.
the NEWeB procedure is a useful and powerful tool for the study of nucleoprotein complexes of plant viruses and similar particles in plant extracts.
the NEWeB technique can be used for the study of the structure and function of different forms of nucleoprotein complexes, not only for PPV but also for other viruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for the characterization of different forms or populations of nucleoprotein complexes that is based on a combination of native electophoresis with immunodetection.
the NEWeB approach is an efficient and reliable method for the characterization of potyviral particles in crude plant extracts.

we have shown that a combination of electrophoretic analysis of nucleoprotein complexes under non-denaturing conditions and Western blotting can be a powerful tool for characterization of different types of virus particles in infected plant tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NEWeB technique allows for the characterization of different forms or populations of nucleoprotein complexes, including virus particles, from infected plants.
NEWeB can be used for the characterization and identification of different forms of plant viruses and similar nucleoproteins.
native electrophoreses is an excellent tool to study the structure of plant viruses.
